posts.name: PlatinumWarlock
posts.cooked:
Pydro:

I have not played it, but I have seen it being compared to Pandemic.

The original edition of Defenders of the Realm does have that feel to a significant degree, but it seems like time and reiteration have begun to make the game more thematic over time. Defenders of the Last Stand (the post-apocalyptic follow-up to DotR) definitely felt more on-theme, and bore much less resemblance to Pandemic than its predecessor. I’d be willing to bet that this moves the general template even further apace.

Does anyone know what relation this game might have to the enigmatic Arkham-Horror-looking prototype that was floating around a few years back? Given Richard Launius’ past involvement with GtG, it wouldn’t surprise me if that prototype evolved into this game.

posts.name: dprcooke
posts.cooked:
I fail to see how it would even remotely be considered even a small 'ha ha' to PW backers.

GTG had a game (Prime War) in development.  It got cancelled because there wasn't a [big enough] market for it.

Unrelatedly, developers not on the GTG staff worked on a game, using their own game system, to be published by a company that is decidedly not GTG.  They appear to be licensing the Sentinels IP.  This new game doesn't seem to involve Prime Aspects fighting it out across multiple realities, so I'm not seeing a connection to PW story-wise.

I'm confused, is GTG simply not allowed to publish anything else Sentinels-related ever again?  Or did they fail to observe some sort of wierd mourning period during which nothing Sentinels can be announced?

Should they have told Arcane Wonders, "we're sorry, we want you to use our IP, but out of respect for our PW backers, we can't let you do anything with it until [insert some future date here]"?

I mean, Sentinels of Freedom got released recently... am I supposed to be insulted or something about that too?
